newsitem.title: UK: LME base metals prices tumble on stop loss selling.
newsitem.headline: LME base metals prices tumble on stop loss selling.

text.p: Base metals prices spiralled downwards on fund-led selling on Thursday, with sharply lower aluminium and zinc leading the way, traders said.

Three months aluminium sank to a low of $1,608 per tonne on the London Metal Exchange (LME), revisiting territory not seen since mid-February. It finished the afternoon kerb at $1,609, a decline of $25.50 from Wednesday.
Traders attributed the steep slide to funds liquidating positions during thin lunch-time trading.
"The liquidation was well signposted," a trader said, noting that aluminium prices had failed to bounce off $1,630 support in recent days.
Sell-stops around $1,620 had been triggered, but further to the downside, $1,600 was the next important support, analysts said.
Zinc also buckled under pressure, having been unable to maintain its grasp on the $1,300 level one day after scoring a fresh 4-1/2 year high of $1,311.
It closed at the day's low of $1,259, a decline of $45 from Wednesday.
"The market had been expecting zinc to try higher after recent good closes, but when the funds tried the downside, the demand just wasn't there," a trader noted.
Prices had bounced from a low $1,260 just before the Easter holiday last week, and another bounce from the area may form a positive "double bottom", some analysts said.
Copper also ended in the minus column at $2,340, a drop of $29 from Wednesday's more positive close. On the downside support was expected at $2,325 and then $2,300, dealers said.
Cash to threes backwardation narrowed to $30/$35, compared to around $40 24 hours earlier.
"All of the metals had a technically bearish close and I'd expect to see more downside tests tomorrow," a trader said.
The other metals were quieter but generally the overall tone was glum.
Lead prices crumbled to close at the day's low of $678, compared to $692.
Cash/threes backwardation was still at a $5/$10 backwardation at the end of the day, however.
Tin held up the best of the lot and finished just $15 easier at $5,850.
Alloy was weaker at $1,515, compared to $1,540 previously. --Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
